Pondra: a streamhouse in one binary. With no command, a SQL shell on a lake

Usage: pondra [LAKE]
       pondra <COMMAND>

Commands:
  serve      Serve a lake, or a folder of lakes as databases: `pondra serve lake`, `pondra serve data`
  service    Keep a node running on this machine: started at boot and again if it stops (systemd, launchd or Windows's service manager). `pondra service install --lake s3://bucket/lake`
  workspace  The lake's files kept in a folder of your own, for git and your editor: `pondra workspace pull ./ws` writes them there, `pondra workspace push ./ws` sends back what changed. A file changed on both sides is listed and left as it is
  init       Start a project in DIR (default: this folder): pondra.toml, objects/, migrations/, seeds/ and tests/. `pondra export` writes one from a database instead (pondra init shop)
  login      Keep a token for each server, for every command after. With no URL: the servers pondra.toml names (pondra login https://pondra.acme.com)
  branch     Start a branch: a Git branch and a database of the same name, prod's data with no file copied (pondra branch add-discounts). With no name, the branches; -d NAME drops one
  switch     Go to a branch that exists, as `git switch` does, and make its database if it isn't there (pondra switch add-discounts)
  plan       What an apply would change in an environment, and why anything is refused (pondra plan test)
  status     What differs between the project's files and an environment, as `git status` does: what an apply would change, what was changed in the database outside an apply, and what no project declares (pondra status)
  capture    Write what was changed in the database outside an apply into the project's files: each object's statement, a migration for a renamed table or column (pondra capture sales.memos)
  apply      Make the project true in an environment: its plan, each step, then its tests (pondra apply test)
  test       Run the project's tests (tests/*.sql: any row back is a failure) in an environment (pondra test test)
  export     An environment's objects as a project's files, in DIR (default: this folder) (pondra export copy --env prod)
  diff       What an environment changes against another: the objects, and the rows of each table both have (`pondra.diff`). Written as Markdown, for a pull request's summary (pondra diff pr-12)
  ci         Continuous integration: `pondra ci init` writes a GitHub Actions workflow for the project (pondra ci init)
  catalog    Print catalog entries whose keys start with `prefix` (t/ tables, s/ segments, p/ producers…)
  sql        Run SQL straight against the lake, no server needed. Queries read the bucket (and local files: `SELECT * FROM 'x.parquet'`). Writes (CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) run here too; the leader records them — over HTTP, or through the bucket if this machine can't reach it — or this process does if nobody leads
  backup     Back a lake up into a lake of its own: `pondra backup s3://b/prod s3://b/backups/prod`. Run again, it copies only what changed since, and keeps what earlier runs need for `--retention-days` (7 by default), so a restore can go back that far. The backup is read like any lake, and written only by its next run. Works with no node running
  restore    Make a lake again from its backup, in a new place: `pondra restore s3://b/backups/prod s3://b/prod2 [--at '2026-10-12 03:00:00']` (its newest run at or before that time, in UTC). Its tasks come back suspended (ALTER TASK name RESUME)
  token      Make a token for a user of a lake, and print it (once: the lake keeps only its hash). Through the bucket, so no token is needed: whoever can write the lake's folder owns it. The lake's first user is `pondra` (made by a node on the network with no token, which prints its token too). `T=$(pondra token --dir lake)`
  run        Run a SQL file — its statements in order, `$name` taking the value of `--name` — on a node of the lake started for it (`pondra run load.sql lake --day 2026-09-27`), or on a node already running (`--url http://host:8080`). `pondra run load.sql --help` lists its parameters
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [LAKE]  With no command: the lake the SQL shell opens (a folder, s3://bucket/prefix, or :memory: for one held in memory until the shell ends; default ./lake)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
